# The radius of the negation of a BallVector: the radius given

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_neg_radius` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$r_x$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r_x).$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_neg_1`, called by `-x` and `neg(x, z)` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)); and of the loop `bv_neg_2`, called by `-x` and `neg(x, z)` of `BallVector<T, 2, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 2>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r_z = \mathrm{RN}(r_x)$: the number of the format nearest to $r_x$, ties to even.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_neg_radius_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvNegMake.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvNegMake.v), against `bv_neg_radius_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_neg_radius_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_neg_radius_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m rx : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  let rz := bv_neg_radius m rx in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  rz = RN emin prec rx.
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `bv_neg_radius_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius of ball_neg_k (Milestone 1 listing), at every entry (milestone2.md, BallVector). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_neg_radius.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_neg_radius.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The one radius of the negation of a BallVector (milestone2.md, "BallVector": bv_neg_k): the radius of
# the operand, unchanged, as ball_neg_k returns it entry by entry. The negation of a center is exact,
# so nothing is added: the result is exactly the set of the negated members. The largest magnitude of
# a center, which every radius kernel of a ball vector takes, is not needed: a canonical operand has
# finite centers or zero ones, and so has its negation.

rz = copy(rx)
```
